page.layout: One column of verse, set in italic, with faint marginal traces on the right. Running head at top. Catchword at lower right. No separate heading.

l.i: Commoda, ciuilesque ciat mala factio motus,
Sic poteris Rex esse diu, populoque praesse,
Quem diuina tibi commisit cura regendum.
Ergo si quis amor, si te qua cura fatiget
Imperii, populique tui, propriaque salutis,
Ne temere admittas inferno Acheronte remensam
Progeniem, rursumque caput, regnumque tuos;
Obuce[?] mille malis, quibus haud virtute resisti,
Nec telis, armisve potest; sat viximus eheu
Pestiferis agitati odiis, scelerumque referti,
Conuenit haud aliunde nouis accersere terris
Foedifragos, tenera deceptoresque iuuenta,
Sat natura mali per se corrupta ministrat.
Cuinam hominum ignotum est IUDAITAS
nocte[?] Nil meditari aliud, quam qua ratione modo
Prisca statuta quoant[?] patriasque euertere leges, Inque
locum, antiquis totum in contraria, nobis
Iura dare, & sanctos priuata ad commoda ritus
Flectere, nulli unquam quod post mutare licebit?
Et te dein placitis cogent subscribere, teque
Pro libitu ad nutum ducent, decretaque condent
Duratura magis quam quae sculpuntur in
are[?], Aut quae Dalmatico fulgent incisa metallo.
Det Deus omnipotens, penes est quae summa potestas,
Inclyte Rex, ne tu, deceptus fraude COTONIS, Melliti alloquio capiare,
æquamque remittas Iram, animumque tuum iustas qui exarsit in iras,
Et poenas merito scelerata a gente poposcit.
Sufficiat lacrymasse tuos, poenasque dedisse[?]
Francigenas toties, dubium haud quin postmodo
nobis Plura ferenda manent mala, qua quæ sensimus olim,

page.notes: Marginal text on the right side (beside most lines) is too faint to read; only the "(dieq" mark near "ministrat." was made out, and it is doubtful. Doubtful readings: "Obuce" (the line runs together with "mille"), "nocte" (the last word of the line appears in a different type), "quoant", "in are", "dedisse". "IUDAITAS" is set in capitals with the vowel u. Long s is written as plain s throughout. The catchword "Aucto-" is at lower right.
